## Celestica’s vision for building what comes next


Artificial intelligence is transforming far more than just the data center—it is fundamentally reshaping how infrastructure is conceived.


For years, progress could be described in terms of individual advances: a faster processor, a denser server, a higher-speed switch, a more efficient storage system. But AI workloads are creating a different kind of challenge. The performance of any one component increasingly depends on everything around it—and on how quickly the complete environment can be brought into operation.


The next advantage will not belong to the organizations that simply acquire the most powerful technology. It will belong to those that can turn that technology into a resilient, scalable, operational system.


That is the opportunity Celestica sees ahead.


## From acceleration to orchestration


AI infrastructure is becoming a new industrial system, shaped by the interaction of compute, data movement, storage, power, thermal management, software and services. Each layer matters. None can be optimized in isolation.


As accelerator density increases, networking must keep data moving. As clusters expand, storage must sustain increasingly parallel workloads. As racks become more powerful, cooling and power architecture become part of system performance. As deployments become more distributed, integration, validation, logistics, serviceability, and asset lifecycle management become essential to business outcomes.


This is why Celestica’s role extends beyond supplying platforms. We help customers connect the decisions that determine whether AI infrastructure performs as designed in the real world.


Our vision is an open, adaptable path from silicon to system, rack to data center, and first deployment through ongoing operations and services. It brings together compute, networking, storage, rack integration, liquid cooling, and lifecycle services in a way that reflects their real-world dependencies.


## Leadership means making complexity usable


The AI infrastructure market does not need more complexity for its own sake. It needs partners that can absorb complexity and make it deployable.


For hyperscalers and neoclouds, that means helping translate ambitious architecture into repeatable, production-ready infrastructure at scale. For enterprises, it means making high-density AI more accessible without requiring every organization to become an infrastructure integrator. For the broader ecosystem, it means advancing open approaches that preserve choice across hardware, software, and deployment models.


Celestica’s leadership is grounded in that connective role. It combines open networking expertise, silicon-to-system co-design, engineering and manufacturing depth, full-rack integration, and end-to-end services. The result is not a collection of disconnected capabilities, but a way to move from design intent to operating reality with greater confidence.


## Unlocking the Open Advantage


At Celestica, designing for what comes next means committing to an open-by-design philosophy across both hardware and software. Through active engagement with the Open Compute Project (OCP), we bring hyperscale-proven design principles to a much broader market, and we pair that open hardware with an open network operating system that is ready for production. Open networking gives operators the flexibility to adapt as AI workloads shift, without relying on a single vendor’s roadmap.


Central to this approach is[SONiC® (Software for Open Networking in the Cloud)](https://sonicfoundation.dev/) , the open-source network operating system that many hyperscalers run their clouds on.[SONiC Plus by Celestica](https://cls.celestica.com/software/celestica-sonic/) is our hardened and qualified distribution of SONiC: the same open foundation, tested end-to-end on Celestica switches with qualified optics and cables, and backed by Celestica support and services. It bridges the gap between open-source innovation and the operational requirements of enterprise, neocloud and hyperscale data centers.


The result is choice without compromise. Operators keep what open networking promises—standard hardware, an open operating system and a broad ecosystem—and gain what production demands: validated releases, one accountable partner for hardware and software, and a release cadence that tracks the SONiC community. That is what turning open design intent into operating reality looks like.


Bringing that operating reality to life requires strong open standards and active ecosystem collaboration. Celestica’s engagement with the open community reflects a belief that the future of AI infrastructure should be built through collaboration, interoperability, and practical innovation—not closed decisions made in isolation. Openness is not an abstract ideal; it is a way to create more flexibility as technology and business requirements change.


## Meet Celestica at OCP Southeast Asia Tech Day


By embracing an open ecosystem, we are not just solving today's challenges; we are building a more flexible, scalable foundation for whatever comes next. Whether you are a hyperscaler, neocloud, or enterprise in the APAC region or beyond, the path to AI infrastructure success is defined by collaboration, interoperability, and the courage to move beyond closed, proprietary models.


Celestica is uniquely positioned to guide you on this path. We offer a truly end-to-end solution, integrating engineering, manufacturing, full-rack systems, and ongoing lifecycle services into a seamless, unified experience. By combining this comprehensive solution offering with our deep commitment to open standards, we empower you to translate design intent into operating reality with greater confidence.


Join us at[OCP Southeast Asia Tech Day](https://www.opencompute.org/summit/2026-ocp-tech-day-dcwa) , Sept 29–30, 2026, Marina Bay Sands, Singapore, Booth #3-B5, to see our latest open hardware innovations and discover how we turn complex open networking into deployable, high-performance solutions.


Don't miss our featured session, "High-Performance AI Fabrics Built on Open Standards: Scaling 800G and 1.6T Infrastructures," presented by Matt Roman, Senior Director of Product Line Management.[Visit our event landing page](https://cls.celestica.com/events/ocp-dcwa26/) for more information on the session and Celestica’s presence at OCP South East Asia. Let's build what's next, together.

AUTHOR BIO


Shankar Vasudevan


Director of Product Management, Networking Software


Shankar Vasudevan is Director of Product Management, Networking Software, at Celestica, where he leads product strategy for SONiC Plus, Celestica's enterprise-grade SONiC network operating system, with a focus on AI data center networking. His background spans the design of Ethernet-based fabrics for the data center, from enterprise environments to the high-performance fabrics behind large-scale AI clusters, together with deep experience in SONiC and open NOS ecosystems and ODM/OEM product strategy. Shankar is based in Chennai, India.
